DLSS 5 for Linux

Neural rendering in your Proton games.
Checked first, then installed.

DLSS 5 for Linux finds your Steam games, says which ones the DLSS 5 neural pass can work in, and installs it with the Proton settings it needs.

  • Will this game work? A probe reads its folder and rates it supported, partial, unsupported or blocked before anything is copied.
  • Online game with anti-cheat? It refuses to install there. This is for single-player games.
  • No game handy? Run the same model over a picture or a video, sound kept. It also tells you when footage is 2D animation, where the model changes little.
  • Made for NVIDIA RTX 40 cards. AMD RX 6000/7000/9000 is experimental; RTX 20, 30 and 50 are not supported yet.

A Linux port of yumlevi's RenoDX DLSS installer. It installs parts it does not ship, each under its own licence: RenoDX, ReShade (BSD-3-Clause), OptiScaler, and NVIDIA's DLSS and Streamline files and model, which are NVIDIA's proprietary software under NVIDIA's licence.
Not affiliated with or endorsed by NVIDIA. DLSS is a trademark of NVIDIA Corporation.

DLSS 5 for Linux on Fedora

One command; dnf downloads the package from the release and what it needs from Fedora:

$ sudo dnf install https://github.com/MiguelCarino/renodx-dlss-installer/releases/download/v0.0.6/dlss5-linux-0.0.6-1.fc44.noarch.rpm

Then open DLSS 5 for Linux from your application menu, or run dlss5-linux-gui. The command line is dlss5-linux --help.

The package has no architecture of its own and installs on current Fedora releases. It also recommends GTK 4, libadwaita and WebKitGTK for the app's own window; without them it opens in your browser. Check the download against SHA256SUMS.

DLSS 5 for Linux AppImage

1. Make it runnable and start it, from the folder you downloaded it to:

$ chmod +x DLSS5_for_Linux-0.0.6-x86_64.AppImage ./DLSS5_for_Linux-0.0.6-x86_64.AppImage

2. Have the usual tools installed. FFmpeg is inside; the rest comes from your system: python3, curl, unzip, binutils, 7-Zip and xdg-utils. On Debian or Ubuntu:

$ sudo apt install python3 curl unzip binutils p7zip-full xdg-utils

3. Pick a game in the app, press Install, and set the launch options it shows in Steam. It opens in its own window when PyGObject with GTK 4, libadwaita and WebKitGTK 6 is installed, and in your browser otherwise.

No FUSE on your system? Add --appimage-extract-and-run after the file name. The command line is the same file followed by cli --help. SHA256SUMS

What it is (and is not)

DLSS 5 for Linux installs NVIDIA's DLSS 5 neural rendering pass into Windows games that run on Linux under Proton, and gives you the launch options they need.

It is for people who play single-player games on Linux. Before it copies anything, a probe reads the game's folder and says whether the pass can work there; it refuses to install where it finds anti-cheat.

It is a Linux port of yumlevi's RenoDX DLSS installer for Windows. It is not made by, affiliated with or endorsed by NVIDIA, and it does not ship NVIDIA's files: the other parts are downloaded from other projects' release pages when you install, and you supply nvngx_dlssnr.dll yourself.

It does not upload anything. Its window is a local page on 127.0.0.1, and pictures and videos are processed on your computer and saved to ~/Pictures/DLSS 5/ and ~/Videos/DLSS 5/.

It needs an NVIDIA RTX 40 card with NVIDIA's driver, and Proton 9 or GE-Proton. AMD RX 6000, 7000 and 9000 are experimental; RTX 20, 30 and 50 are not supported yet. Expect a large frame-rate cost: about 39% has been reported on RTX 40.

Features

  • Finds your games in every Steam library, and takes GOG, Heroic, Epic or other Wine game folders you add by hand.
  • A probe rates each game supported, feeder, amd, partial, unsupported, blocked or unknown before anything is installed.
  • Four engines: OptiScaler (the default), ReShade with RenoDX, a feeder for games with no DLSS of their own, and an experimental one for AMD GPUs.
  • Install, uninstall and launch from the app. A reinstall keeps the settings you changed.
  • Says whether it ran: the app reads the injector's log and tells you if the neural pass was actually dispatched.
  • F9 in game turns the neural pass on and off.
  • Images & video (experimental): run the same model on a picture or a video, sound kept, and see whether it is 2D animation, where the model changes little.
  • A command line, dlss5-linux, with --dry-run to print every change before it happens and --install-proton to fetch the latest GE-Proton.
